correctness.rationale: Orthogonality gives a q^-2 pair-sum energy, and the exact (u+v,u^3+v^3) fiber classification holds for all characteristic >3. The zero-sum collision is counted once, including the origin diagonal. Each antipodal pair reduces to t_j,b_j, with independent Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle bounds. The reduced F(a,B) is strictly convex in B, its endpoints are maximized exactly, and equality forces squared masses in ratio 3:2 and phase-aligned antipodal products. Direct convolution, independent energy formula, phase extremizers, and GF25 field arithmetic were checked by packaged verify.py (200 random trials and five sharpness instances). Computation does not replace universal algebra.

originality.rationale: The actual studied parameter is the sharp L2-to-L4 operator norm and all nonzero maximizers on (u,u^3). Three primary full texts and multiple published-finding corpus queries were compared for genuine implication. The all-curves result gives only nonsharp exponent boundedness; quadratic surfaces and full moment curves have different pair-sum fibers, while the closest indexed quartic-graph record provides only constant-input energy. No known compared result supplies the exact norm 3-6/(2q+1) or its antipodal equality family; unindexed equivalents are an acknowledged residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named exact cubic-graph restriction theorem may already supply the same sharp constant and extremizers.
The checked literature and indexed record search cannot certify global novelty across unpublished or inaccessible work.

value.rationale: This determines the exact sharp endpoint constant and all extremizers on the natural plane cubic monomial graph for every finite field of characteristic >3. Unlike the general boundedness theorem, the result quantifies a nontrivial optimal improvement and an exceptional amplitude profile caused by the noninjective antipodal pair-sum fiber. Constant inputs are strictly suboptimal by (q-1)/(q^2(2q+1)), so the classification is not a routine evaluation of unweighted additive energy. The explicit optimizer family is useful for distinguishing degenerate monomial dispersions from quadratic finite-field restriction problems.
